title: EA-CORPORA-27 — The Twenty-Seventh Seating: Spinoza, Leibniz's Monadology, Nietzsche, Bergson, Kafka and Artaud, Each in Its Original Language, Beside the Declared Absence of Deleuze and Guattari
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Seven seats on the originals shelf for the sources Deleuze and Guattari read, each in its original language, beside their own declared absence. Spinoza: the Ethica, the Tractatus de intellectus emendatione, the Tractatus politicus and the Tractatus theologico-politicus in Latin (van Vloten and Land, 1882). Leibniz: the Monadology alone, in French, in its first printing (Erdmann, 1840) and Piat's edition (1900). Nietzsche: eight books in German as printed in his lifetime (1876–1895) with six transcriptions. Bergson: the Essai (1889), Matière et mémoire (1896), Le Rire (1900) and Durée et simultanéité (1922) in their first editions. Kafka: eight works in German as first published (1912–1925). Artaud: the correspondence with Jacques Rivière (La Nouvelle Revue française, 1924) and L'Art et la mort (1929). Deleuze and Guattari: fourteen works named with their rights holders and the dates they open, and no text. What is not seated, and why, is named.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Sources located, fetched, checked against the Internet Archive's published md5 sums and against their title pages, assembled into seats, hashed and indexed, and the loci found in the seated text, all in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction. The request (Deleuze and Guattari's sources, and the Monadology only) and the declared absence are Lee Sharks's; the witnesses were chosen in session and are stated per seat. methodology: Sources located on the Internet Archive and on Project Gutenberg; each item's title page read against the edition claimed for it, with nothing asserted beyond it. Internet Archive files checked against the Archive's md5. Every file hashed into its seat's MANIFEST.sha256. Loci are strings found in the seated text by rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-27/seat.py. Licences stated per seat (payload/record split). The builders, the specifications and this body are under rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-27/.
falsification_conditions: A seat is falsified if its files do not verify against its MANIFEST.sha256 at the canonical URL; if a seated Internet Archive file's md5 differs from the Archive's; if a Project Gutenberg file differs from the eBook number recorded for it; if an edition statement misstates the title page of the file it describes; if a verified locus cannot be found in the seated text; if an item stated public domain in the United States is not; if a date of opening declared in 27/07 misstates the term it follows; or if the four surfaces (seat, index, deposit, shelf) disagree.

wiki_article: EA-CORPORA-27 is the twenty-seventh seating of primary sources on the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's originals shelf, deposited by Lee Sharks on 27 October 2026. It seats, each in the language it was written in, the sources Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari read and wrote books upon, beside a seat that declares their own works absent. Spinoza (27/01) is held in Latin in J. van Vloten and J. P. N. Land's edition of 1882: the Ethica, the Tractatus de intellectus emendatione, the Tractatus politicus and the Tractatus theologico-politicus. Leibniz (27/02) is held in the Monadology alone, at the operator's word, in its first printing in French (J. E. Erdmann, Opera philosophica, 1840) and in Clodius Piat's edition (1900). Nietzsche (27/03) is held in eight books in German as printed in his lifetime, from Richard Wagner in Bayreuth (1876) to Also sprach Zarathustra (1895), with six transcriptions. Bergson (27/04) is held in the first editions of the Essai sur les données immédiates de la conscience (1889), Matière et mémoire (1896), Le Rire (1900) and Durée et simultanéité (1922). Kafka (27/05) is held in eight works in German as first published, from Betrachtung (1912) to Der Prozess (1925). Artaud (27/06) is held in his correspondence with Jacques Rivière in La Nouvelle Revue française (1924) and L'Art et la mort (1929). The seventh seat, for Deleuze and Guattari, holds no text: it names fourteen works, from Empirisme et subjectivité (1953) to Chaosmose (1992), with their publishers and the dates they open, in France in 2063 and 2066 and in the United States between 2049 and 2088. The seating was asked for when the operator found no way around their copyright: "yes - i cant believe we havent seated spinoza yet. yes to all." Spinoza's first editions are queued, the open scans found being unreadable or under a commercial copyright notice.
